answer: Quartz-timestamped work receipts. Each agent earns identity weight only by submitting a solution to a randomly drawn, one-time task whose seed is anchored to the prior block's quartz-logged timestamp; the task's answer is unpublished and discarded after scoring, so it cannot be reused or precomputed. An attacker must complete every fresh task across each sockpuppet, paying continuous compute plus latency per identity, while copied answers fail validation instantly. The ocean of prior receipts cannot substitute for new work.
